paper_id: Exploring Data-Efficient Adaptation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
title: Exploring Data-Efficient Adaptation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
motivation: LLMs struggle in specific code generation scenarios where limited training data leads to poor performance
problem_framing: How to effectively adapt LLMs with few training samples while avoiding performance degradation
key_insight: Revised code from error corrections is closer in model representation space (6.39) than original dataset samples (12.35), enabling more efficient learning
method_signature: DEED: Error-driven four-step loop (collect errors → Self-Revise → optimize → iterate)
evaluation_criteria: Pass@k via test case execution on HumanEval, MBPP, DataScience benchmarks
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Self-refine and Self-debug underperform on small LLMs; full fine-tuning is computationally expensive
evidence_for_taste: compelling LLMs to relearn is inefficient
error-driven learning requires learners to identify errors
Raise a Child in Large Language Model
thinking_moves: 把人从错误中学习的认知机制迁移到模型适应
用表示空间的距离度量论证为何纠错样本比原始样本更有效
把主流微调批为低效：要求模型重新学习完整样本而非针对性修正
迭代优化而非一次性微调以实现持续改进
cites_own_work: [73] Self-Edit: Fault-Aware Code Editor for Code Generation
